expect: Missed trigger, Warning: your opponent chooses whether Ball Lightning's trigger goes on the stack now (IPG 2.1).

text: I forgot the Hellrider trigger while attacking. What happens?
expect: Missed trigger, no penalty: your opponent chooses whether Hellrider's trigger goes on the stack now (IPG 2.1).

text: I forgot to scry. What happens?
expect: No infraction: by the MTR 4.2 shortcut, a player who doesn't scry when told to is assumed to have chosen not to look and to leave the cards in the same order.

text: My opponent forgot their Dark Confidant trigger. We noticed after they drew. What happens?
expect: Missed trigger, no penalty: you choose whether Dark Confidant's trigger goes on the stack now (IPG 2.1).

text: I missed my Phyrexian Arena trigger last turn. What happens now?
expect: Missed trigger, no penalty: if the game is now past this turn's beginning phase, the game just continues and the trigger is gone; if not, your opponent chooses whether Phyrexian Arena's trigger goes on the stack now (IPG 2.1).

text: At an RCQ my opponent forgot to sacrifice their Ball Lightning. Do they get a penalty?
expect: Yes. Missed trigger, Warning: you choose whether Ball Lightning's trigger goes on the stack now (IPG 2.1).

text: I forgot my Sheoldred, the Apocalypse trigger three turns ago. Can I still get the life?
expect: No: it's missed for good, no penalty: it was missed before the current phase of the previous turn, so the game just continues and the trigger is gone (IPG 2.1).

text: My opponent missed their Pact of Negation trigger at FNM. Do they lose?
expect: It depends: at Regular REL, the judge puts Pact of Negation's trigger on the stack now, unless that would be too disruptive (not if significant decisions were made based on it not happening) — and then your opponent pays {3}{U}{U} or loses the game.

text: I forgot the Flickerwisp return trigger at the end step. We noticed during my opponent's upkeep. What happens?
expect: Missed trigger, no penalty: Flickerwisp's delayed trigger ("Return that card to the battlefield under its owner's control at the beginning of the next end step") still happens; your opponent chooses whether it resolves now or when a player would get priority at the start of the next phase (IPG 2.1).

text: I didn't remember my Bitterblossom trigger in my upkeep and drew for the turn. What's the ruling?
expect: Missed trigger, no penalty: your opponent chooses whether Bitterblossom's trigger goes on the stack now (IPG 2.1).

text: Is it a missed trigger if I forget Ragavan's dash return?
expect: Yes: it's a missed trigger, Warning, and Ragavan, Nimble Pilferer's delayed trigger ("It's returned from the battlefield to its owner's hand at the beginning of the next end step") still happens: your opponent chooses whether it resolves now or when a player would get priority at the start of the next phase.

text: I forgot to put a lore counter on my Saga. What's the penalty?
expect: Missed trigger, no penalty: your opponent chooses whether the lore counter is put on now (IPG 2.1).

text: My opponent forgot their exalted trigger and said take two. Do I have to point it out?
expect: No: you never have to point out your opponent's triggers; not reminding them is neither Failure to Maintain Game State nor Cheating (MTR 4.5, IPG 2.6).

text: I accidentally drew 2 extra cards. What's the penalty at an RCQ?
expect: Hidden Card Error, Warning: you reveal your hand and your opponent chooses 2 cards from it that they didn't already know; they go back into the library, shuffled into its random portion (IPG 2.3).

text: My opponent drew an extra card at FNM. What happens?
expect: No penalty at Regular REL: 1 card is taken at random from their hand and put on top of their library, without shuffling it (JAR).

text: I cast Ancestral Recall and drew four cards. What's the fix?
expect: Hidden Card Error, Warning: you reveal your hand and your opponent chooses 1 card from it that they didn't already know; it goes back into the library, shuffled into its random portion (IPG 2.3).

text: I drew 9 cards for my opening hand. What happens?
expect: Mulligan Procedure Error, Warning: you take an additional mulligan (IPG 2.4).

text: I accidentally flipped over the top card of my library. What's the penalty?
expect: Looking at Extra Cards, Warning: the card you saw is shuffled into the random portion of the library, and any cards whose positions were already known go back to their places (IPG 2.2).

text: My opponent forgot to untap their lands. What happens?
expect: Game Rule Violation, Warning: it's still the same turn, so your opponent untaps them now (IPG 2.5's partial fix for a forgotten untap).

text: I played two lands this turn at FNM. What happens?
expect: Game Rule Violation, Warning: caught right away, a simple backup returns the second land to hand; later, it goes back to hand only if that's a minor disruption (an object in the wrong zone that everyone can identify), otherwise the game is left as it is (IPG 2.5).

text: My opponent cast Lightning Bolt without paying for my Thalia at an RCQ. What's the penalty?
expect: Game Rule Violation, Warning: Thalia, Guardian of Thraben's ability is static, not a trigger (604.1), so nothing was missed; your opponent committed it by casting Lightning Bolt without paying Thalia, Guardian of Thraben's extra cost (IPG 2.5).

text: I was 15 minutes late for my match. What happens?
expect: Tardiness, Match Loss: not in your seat 10 minutes into the round, you lose the match and are dropped from the tournament, unless you report to the Head Judge or Scorekeeper before the round ends (IPG 3.1).

text: My opponent was 3 minutes late. What's the penalty?
expect: Tardiness, Game Loss: 3 minutes late, your opponent loses a game, and the match gets a 3-minute time extension (IPG 3.1).

text: Do I have to tell my opponent how many cards are in my hand at FNM?
expect: Yes: at Regular REL derived information, like the number of cards in a hand, counts as free, so you must answer completely and honestly (MTR 4.1).

text: Can I ask my opponent what their card does?
expect: Yes, ask — but at Competitive REL your opponent doesn't have to explain it: what a card does is derived information. You're entitled to its official Oracle text, so call a judge to read it to you (MTR 3.6, 4.1).

text: Can I lie about my life total?
expect: No: your life total is status information, and no player may represent it incorrectly (MTR 4.1); lying about it on purpose to gain an advantage is Cheating, a Disqualification (IPG 4.8).

text: I said "go" and then wanted to play a land. Can I?
expect: No: by saying "go" you passed priority, and your opponent is now assumed to be acting in your end step (MTR 4.2); a land can be played only in your main phase (305.2).

text: My opponent says "go to combat". Can I still cast a sorcery?
expect: No: it's your opponent's turn, and a sorcery can be cast only in your own main phase (307.1). By the shortcut you're now acting in their beginning of combat step, so you can cast instants and activate abilities there (MTR 4.2).

text: I said "go to combat". Can my opponent cast an instant before attackers?
expect: Yes: "go to combat" passes priority in your main phase, and by the shortcut your opponent is then acting in the beginning of combat step, before attackers are declared (MTR 4.2). After that you get priority there too.

text: My opponent forgot to shuffle after fetching. What happens?
expect: Insufficient Shuffling, Warning: the library is shuffled thoroughly now (IPG 3.9).

text: I forgot to discard down to seven. What happens?
expect: Game Rule Violation, Warning: you discard down to seven now: a player who failed to discard does so (IPG 2.5's partial fix).

text: Do I have to remind my opponent about their Sheoldred trigger?
expect: No: you never have to point out your opponent's triggers; not reminding them is neither Failure to Maintain Game State nor Cheating (MTR 4.5, IPG 2.6).

text: My opponent rushed through their upkeep before I could announce my trigger. Is it missed?
expect: No: your opponent can't make your trigger be missed by rushing ahead; if you acknowledge it before you take an active role (an action, or explicitly passing priority), it's remembered (IPG 2.1).
